newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds slip, but spreads narrower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds slip, but spreads narrower.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities recorded modest losses on Thursday, dipping lightly after the weekly jobless claims report.
Despite the losses, mortgage spreads generally narrowed over Treasuries.
"There's been better buying in mortgages, and consequently they tightened pretty well," one trader said. "There's been retail buying generally, but no huge program trades."
On Thursday morning the Commerce Department said initial jobless claims fell to 320,000 in the week ended October 19 from a revised 342,000 the previous week.
Treasuries slipped as much as half a point after the data but recovered some early losses in the afternoon.
The credit markets were more sensitive to claims than usual because the week's economic calendar has been so sparse, traders said. "There's just been no news," said one.

Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 1/32 at 99-15/32, yielding 107 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae paper was off 1/32 at 99/13-32, and Freddie Mac current coupons were off 1/32 at 99-18/32.
The 10-year Treasury note had climbed 4/32 to 99-16/32, yielding 6.57 percent.
